summary: WebSocket-controlled PTY grants remote shell over the host
details: On agent startup the package connects to a configured WebSocket server (default `ws://localhost:3456`, overridable via SERVER_URL to any remote host) and routes server-sent messages into local host operations. The `terminal_input` handler writes server-supplied bytes directly into a spawned PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), and other handlers perform arbitrary file read/write and git operations under the user's identity. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket server therefore holds shell-level control of the machine running the agent. In addition, startup unconditionally `git clone`s and `git pull --ff-only`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git on the mutable `main` branch, chmod +x's the hook scripts, copies them under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, and sets `enabledPlugins[yeaft-skills@yeaft-skills-dev] = true` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so any future content on that repo's HEAD runs as Claude Code hooks with user privileges. The default WebSocket target is localhost, but the SERVER_URL override and the network→PTY wiring make the mechanism a general-purpose remote-shell channel.
